author: _Gill
body:
I think Slack should be flushed down the toilet.

There, I said it. And I know its some innovative Skype type thing where you have a community and whatnot. Ive used it, and its not super special in my opinion. But this isn't the reason it is killing this server. Slack causes basically a language barrier between the community and staff, which kills interactions between these two intertwined societies.

I attempted to communicate to the Sr Staff team before (yes, this was a while ago). I sent them messages containing troll accounts, hackers, etc (all with evidence). Turns out 0% of the Sr Staff had checked their Skype, so I gave up. It was really disheartening when I couldn't even talk to the people who run the server.

Possibly a middle point would be to keep Slack for just Staff related conversations and whatnot, but I think it should be mandatory to have Skype and at least check it once every 2 days.

Here are the Pro's and Con's of both of these forms of communication.

Slack Pro's:
Less spam
Better platform
No annoying players to respond to

Slack Con's: 
0 Communication the the 99% of Avicus
Players getting angry because they can't talk to Staff members

Skype Pro's:
Everyone has access to the free service and can message anyone
Decent platform (improving)

Skype Con's:
Spammers (but there is a block button.)
Annoying players


Please give feedback on this topic, and if you disagree with anything, feel free to respond (politely)

Thank you for reading,
Max

replies.author: keenanjt
replies.body:
I for one prefer email, so I tell people to contact me that way. For others, Skype is just fine. Many, I'd venture to guess, simply would rather communicate through Avicus' services (MC, TS, forums), which is a-ok. Slack is just there to handle internal communication safely and securely, something Skype will never do, because it wasn't designed for teams. This is the reason we originally switched. As for the senior staff, email, in addition to Avicus' services, is the official way to communicate.

Requiring Skype? I don't support this because in many ways it would be similar to forcing staff to give out their phone number, requiring them to answer texts and calls. Granted, that's more extreme, but it still is extending past what is necessary in my opinion. We're an MC server after all, why should we require our staff to lend themselves useful aside from the server?

I'm not sure if this Englished properly, it's late.
